description: Cloud CRM and business platform with sales, service, marketing, commerce, and data products.
self_serve_details: A free Developer Edition org is documented for testing/development. API use requires the API Enabled permission and an OAuth client app configured within the org; this does not establish free production API access for every customer plan.
blocker: Org-scoped OAuth/client-app setup and API permission; production access depends on the target org and plan.

description: Customer relationship platform and CRM for contact management, deals, sales activity, pipeline management, and related customer data.
self_serve_details: A free CRM account can be created without a credit card and has no expiration. API credentials are account-scoped: creating legacy private apps requires super-admin access; app scopes and rate limits depend on account entitlements and subscription. Public/multi-account applications use OAuth.
blocker: Account-specific scopes, super-admin setup for private tokens, and plan-dependent features/quotas; public OAuth apps require developer-platform app configuration.

description: Sales CRM for managing leads, deals, contacts, sales pipelines, and related sales activity.
self_serve_details: Users can obtain a personal API token from the Pipedrive app when the company permission set enables API use. Public Marketplace integrations use OAuth and registered app credentials; developer sandbox access is requested through the Developer Hub form. The official pages opened do not settle production-plan pricing eligibility.
blocker: The user's Pipedrive account must permit app installation and the user's Pipedrive role/visibility governs access; this documented ChatGPT connection also requires a Pro, Business, Enterprise, or Edu ChatGPT plan (a separate provider-plan gate). Public Marketplace apps require registered OAuth and user authorization.

description: Customizable, data-driven CRM with developer APIs and workspace-level record, object, list, and activity management.
self_serve_details: Attio offers a Free plan (up to three seats; the pricing page says no credit card is required) and lists API/webhook access and MCP across plan tiers. Users can connect to the hosted MCP through OAuth under their own workspace permissions; workspace API-key creation remains admin-only and scoped.
blocker: For REST API keys, a workspace admin must issue a scoped token; OAuth/MCP operations remain limited to the authorizing user's workspace permissions/scopes, and MCP writes require confirmation.

description: Open-source CRM with managed cloud and self-hosted deployments, custom objects, and extensible data/workflow features.
self_serve_details: Twenty offers self-hosting and a self-serve managed-cloud trial; the official pricing page lists paid Cloud Pro/Organization plans and Enterprise sales, with API, webhooks, and MCP included for the listed Cloud plans. Cloud trial/ongoing plan and self-hosting infrastructure are different access paths.
blocker: Cloud access is trial/plan-based and usage quotas vary by plan; self-hosted deployments require operator setup and API credentials.

description: Flexible work-management platform for customizable team workspaces, workflows, collaboration, and lead/project tracking.
self_serve_details: Podio's official developer FAQ says API use is available to free and paid accounts without an API fee, and users can sign up/sign in and create API keys in account settings. Base rate limits apply; higher limits require an account add-on, and some programmatic app-token/elevated-trust paths require contacting support.
blocker: Base rate limits; elevated throughput and some programmatic app-token or high-trust operations require add-on or support interaction.

description: Cloud CRM for managing leads, contacts, accounts, deals, and sales workflows, with API and AI-agent tooling.
self_serve_details: Zoho CRM's official API limits include a Free Edition with 5,000 API credits per rolling 24-hour window. Developers register a client in Zoho's API Console, obtain OAuth tokens, and request user permission; quotas, scopes, roles, and edition limits still apply. Zoho CRM also publishes first-party OAuth MCP servers, which consume the same API credits.
blocker: OAuth/account role permissions and edition-specific API credits/concurrency limits; MCP calls share the same quota.

description: Sales CRM for leads, contacts, opportunities, calling, email, SMS, sales activity, and pipeline workflows.
self_serve_details: Close offers a 14-day trial without a credit card and paid subscription tiers. API keys are created in account settings; OAuth is available for user-facing/public integrations. MCP supports OAuth 2.0 dynamic client registration and also scoped API-key access.
blocker: A Close account/subscription is required beyond the limited trial; MCP/API write and destructive scopes need explicit authorization.

description: Google Workspace-oriented CRM for contacts, sales leads, opportunities, pipelines, tasks, and client/project work.
self_serve_details: Copper offers a self-serve trial; API keys are generated from the Copper web app by an admin and used with the owner email. OAuth 2.0 is the preferred route for partner integrations, but official OAuth quickstart says the application must be registered and client credentials obtained by contacting Copper. Current API entitlement by plan was not resolved from the opened pricing matrix.
blocker: Account-admin API-key setup, partner contact for OAuth client credentials, and unresolved plan-level API entitlement.

description: Deal and relationship intelligence platform for professional firms, including pipeline, contact, firm, and investment/deal management.
self_serve_details: DealCloud API access is tenant-specific. An organization administrator must enable the API capability for the user's group; the user then enables/copies an API key in their profile. API documentation directs users without admin access to their organization's administrator or DealCloud Customer Success Manager. First-party MCP additionally requires DealCloud with Celeste licensing and admin/user MCP permissions.
blocker: Requires a provisioned customer tenant and system-admin/API capability; MCP use additionally requires the Celeste license and MCP permissions.

description: Customer-service platform with Support ticketing for tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and ticket workflows.
self_serve_details: Zendesk lists self-serve trials and paid Support/Suite plans. API requests require a verified user; OAuth access is instance-bound, while public multi-customer integrations must use a global OAuth client. The opened pricing page does not map API access to a specific trial or plan, so a free-credential conclusion is not assigned.
blocker: Verified account access and OAuth client setup are required; public distribution requires global OAuth. Plan-to-API entitlement and official MCP availability remain unresolved.

description: Customer-service platform for support conversations, messaging, shared inboxes, tickets, and customer data, with Fin AI features.
self_serve_details: Intercom offers self-serve trial signup, but the official Conversations API reference says the API is available only to apps with a trial or active subscription. Plan, usage, and API scope conditions still apply; the pricing page does not state trial duration in the opened text.
blocker: A workspace trial or active subscription is needed for the Conversations API; public apps use OAuth, and MCP is unavailable for AU-hosted workspaces.

description: Customer-support helpdesk for ticketing, shared inboxes, customer portals, knowledge bases, and agent workflows.
self_serve_details: The current Freshdesk support plan matrix marks API-key functionality unavailable on Free and available on Growth, Pro, and Enterprise. Pricing offers self-serve trial entry for paid plans, but trial entitlements were not tested. Freshdesk MCP is generally available on Growth, Pro, and Enterprise with plan-based action allowances and optional action packs.
blocker: Free excludes API access; verified API-key/role access, paid-tier rate limits, and the Freshdesk MCP action allowance/add-on structure constrain deployment.

description: Customer-operations platform with a shared inbox and APIs for syncing, retrieving, creating, updating, and deleting conversations and related resources.
self_serve_details: Front provides a free developer environment for API work, limited to three teammates. API tokens are a quick path for an internal/single-customer integration; public integrations must use OAuth unless Front grants an exception. Public partnership/listing is a separate process.
blocker: Public integrations require OAuth; Front MCP is open beta and requires a client ID/secret (no DCR). Tools inherit the user's role and scopes.

description: B2B customer-support platform with programmatic access to customer accounts, issues, contacts, messages, and related support data.
self_serve_details: Official API and support docs establish API/MCP credentials inside an existing Pylon workspace, but the reviewed pricing URL repeatedly redirected to a demo-booking page. A public signup/trial path and the precise plan entitlement for API/MCP therefore remain unresolved.
blocker: REST tokens require a Pylon Admin; MCP requires a Member/Admin OAuth login and cannot use machine credentials. Account/trial/plan entitlement remains unknown.

description: Helpdesk and customer-support suite with ticketing, live chat, knowledge base, automation, and call-center features.
self_serve_details: LiveAgent advertises a 30-day no-credit-card trial and paid per-agent tiers. Its hosted MCP tools count against the account's AI-credit budget; the current API v3 reference is available from within a customer account, so the trial does not by itself prove every API operation or entitlement.
blocker: The server URL is tenant-specific, agent role permissions apply, MCP uses AI credits, and the current v3 API reference is account-gated.

description: Support platform for customer-service teams with thread, customer, tenant, and workflow data exposed through GraphQL and agent tooling.
self_serve_details: Plain advertises a seven-day free trial with no credit card and self-serve Foundation pricing. API credentials require a workspace machine user and explicitly selected permissions; the opened pricing table does not reliably map every API/MCP capability to each tier.
blocker: A workspace and machine-user permission setup are required for API keys; hosted MCP requires interactive OAuth and client support for token refresh/scopes. Plan mapping is incomplete.

description: Customer-support platform with a shared inbox, conversations, customer records, knowledge bases, workflows, and reporting.
self_serve_details: Help Scout's API and MCP access is included on Standard, Plus, and Pro plans; the official pricing page also lists a separate Free plan. The MCP guide says new connections are read-only; Reports require Plus/Pro and Docs knowledge-base tools need a separate Docs API key.
blocker: Paid Standard/Plus/Pro entitlement and an active invited user are required; MCP is read-only, reports need Plus/Pro, and Docs has a separate API key.

description: Customer-support helpdesk for ecommerce teams, with ticketing and an AI Agent available alongside the support inbox.
self_serve_details: Gorgias offers self-serve trial signup and paid helpdesk plans. Its API credentials are available on Helpdesk plans to owners/admins; the official first-party MCP is included at no extra cost for paid plan customers and remains open beta in the reviewed announcement.
blocker: API keys require owner/admin access and grant full account data; public apps require OAuth2; the official MCP is paid-plan-only and open beta.

description: Customer-service platform with a REST API for customer profiles, conversations, messages, tasks, answers, reports, and related support workflows.
self_serve_details: Gladly's official company blog labels its product pricing as Custom (sales-led), while the homepage offers Get a Demo/Try it yourself; neither establishes an API-specific commercial entitlement. For an existing instance, an administrator must grant API User permission before an agent can create/use a token. Sandbox access requires purchasing/contacting a CSM or support team.
blocker: Requires an existing Gladly tenant and administrator-granted API User permission; sandbox testing is separately purchased/contact-mediated. MCP availability is unknown.
